chunks.content: ## Opening and Importing Files in CLO This section explains how to locate and import specific files such as Knife Plates and Fibonacci patterns into CLO's 2D and 3D windows for pleat addition and garment manipulation. - Open the **Printed Files** folder. - Locate the **F Adding Plates** in the Scene Details. - Double-click on **Knife Plates** or drag it directly into the **2D** or **3D window**. - Enter the **Fibonacci** file name and drag it into both the **2D** and **3D windows**. These imported elements serve as the base for pleat creation and manipulation in the garment design. --- ## Using Flare and Center Blur Tools for Pleat Preparation This section details the use of the Flare tool to lock flare lines and the Center Blur tool to refine foundational lines before pleat folding. - Lock a line using the **Flare tool** to define flare boundaries. - In the **2D toolbar**, select the **Center Blur Tool**. - Select all foundation lines from the **2D window**. - Set the baseline to the **inner line** to establish fold reference points. This process prepares the fabric's base structure for accurate pleat folding. --- ## Setting Fold Directions with the Fold and Fold Tool This section covers how to use the **Fold and Fold tool** to define fold directions and apply pleats on skirt panels. - In the **2D toolbar**, select the **Fold and Fold tool**. - Set the fold direction by clicking next to the skirt panel in the 2D window and moving the mouse. - The arrow follows the mouse movement, indicating where the fold will occur. - Pass the arrow through the entire skirt panel. - Double-click to complete the fold direction setting. - When the fold settings window appears, select **Follow** and click **OK**. - Repeat the process for the back of the skirt panel. This ensures the pleats are correctly oriented and consistent on both front and back skirt panels. --- ## Executing Complex Fold Operations on the Belt and Button Areas This section explains folding techniques specific to detailed garment sections such as the belt and single buttons. - Use the **Fold and Fold tool** to start folding on a belt section. - Press again to complete the first half of the fold. - For the second part of the fold (e.g., seven points on the single button), select the boxes at the end of the fold section. - Press again when the fold details are complete. - Ensure folds are aligned and follow the thickening direction of the fold. - Use **Return to Countdown** if needed to correct fold sequence. This technique allows precise control over complex folds in detailed garment components. --- ## Panel Selection, Arrangement, and Manipulation This section describes selecting, arranging, and manipulating panels in 2D and 3D views for pleat adjustments. - Use the **Line Selection tool** to divide panels into sections.

chunks.content: - Press again when the fold details are complete. - Ensure folds are aligned and follow the thickening direction of the fold. - Use **Return to Countdown** if needed to correct fold sequence. This technique allows precise control over complex folds in detailed garment components. --- ## Panel Selection, Arrangement, and Manipulation This section describes selecting, arranging, and manipulating panels in 2D and 3D views for pleat adjustments. - Use the **Line Selection tool** to divide panels into sections. - In the **3D vertical toolbar**, select the 4th panel and click the display point to highlight the model with blue points. - Select all panels in the **2D window** by pressing **Ctrl + A**. - Move panels up and down or arrange them around the virtual model using the purple bar. - Hide or show display points as needed. - Paste individual panels by selecting them in the 2D window and performing paste actions in the virtual machine. This workflow facilitates precise panel positioning around the 3D garment model. --- ## Hardening Panels to Enhance Folding Performance This section describes hardening panels to temporarily increase their stiffness, improving fold accuracy and speed. - In the **2D window**, select front and back panels by holding **Shift**. - Right-click on the panels in the **3D window** and select **Harden** from the menu. - Hardened panels temporarily increase in rigidity, allowing faster and more precise folding. - Activate the model to see the folding effect immediately. Hardening is useful when working on pleats to maintain panel shape during manipulation. --- ## Unhazing Panels to View Final Skirt Strength This section explains how to remove haze effects from panels to better visualize skirt strength and final appearance. - Select all skirt panels. - Drag the touch icon (likely referring to a UI element) to the menu. - Select **Unhaze panel** to remove haze. - Activate the model to observe the true strength and finish of the skirt panels. Unhazing allows designers to assess the visual and structural effect of pleats clearly. --- # Summary This tutorial segment guides users through importing pleat-related files, preparing fabric lines with flare and blur tools, setting fold directions, executing complex folds, manipulating panels in 2D and 3D views, hardening panels to aid folding, and unhazing panels to finalize skirt appearance in CLO. The use of specific tools like Fold and Fold, Flare, Center Blur, and panel hardening techniques optimize the pleating process for realistic garment simulation.
